references.text: Balak built seven altars as Balaam had requested, which explains the context of the offering in verse 2.
Balak repeats the same sacrificial practice with seven bulls and seven rams at another location, showing a pattern in his attempts to get Balaam to curse Israel.
Balak sacrifices bulls and rams again in the same way, demonstrating his persistent effort to influence God through offerings.
Balak had previously sacrificed cattle and small livestock, showing his willingness to use sacrifices to achieve his goals.
Abraham offered a ram instead of Isaac, illustrating the use of rams as sacrificial animals in important contexts.
A bull and a ram were used as a peace offering, reflecting the common practice of sacrificing these animals together.
